newsitem.title: CHINA: China non-state bank opens Shanghai branch.
newsitem.headline: China non-state bank opens Shanghai branch.

text.p: The first Chinese non-state bank set up since 1949 has opened a branch in Shanghai, official media reported on Sunday.

China Minsheng Bank was founded in January, 1996, with share capital of 1.38 billion yuan from 59 members of the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce, the country's largest alliance of non-state firms.
At the opening of the Shanghai branch on Saturday, the bank signed agreements with 10 companies to provide loans totalling 120 million yuan, the Shanghai Securities News said.
On Saturday, the bank also made a donation of 200,000 yuan to the Shanghai Charity Foundation, the newspaper said.
China Minsheng is the 15th Chinese bank to open a branch in Shanghai, the Liberation Daily newspaper said.
China Minsheng opened a branch in the southern city of Guangzhou a few days ago and plans to open more in developed areas of China in 1997, the Xinhua news agency said.
Bank officials have said they aim to provide 70 percent of their loans to non-state companies.
